clue.text: Dead shy in disposition-in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: a disposition is an arrangement, so the letters of the three words before it are set out afresh

explanation.surface: Someone very timid by nature, described in a roundabout way of talking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposition' looks like a noun for temperament, but it signals the anagram of DEAD SHY IN; the second 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Hendiadys is a figure of speech expressing one idea through two words joined by 'and', such as 'nice and warm'.

clue.text: No longer cheeky to the master

parts.note: ex- describes something former, no longer so
pert means impudent or saucy

explanation.surface: A pupil who has stopped being rude to the schoolmaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the' is a link joining wordplay to definition; 'master' is a skilled person here, not a teacher.
explanation.definitionFit: A master of a craft is a highly skilled practitioner, a synonym.

clue.text: Involve others because of a minor setback at home

parts.note: a drawn match is only a small disappointment for a team expecting to win
someone in is at home

explanation.surface: Bringing other people into it because of a small reverse at one's home ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a football team drawing a home game; the pieces are joined by the link 'because of'.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw someone in is to get them involved or entangled in an affair, a phrasal synonym.

clue.text: Father gets upset by pain, but he's brave

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so in this down answer the word for father reads upwards

parts.note: Pa is an informal word for father
an ache is a dull pain

explanation.surface: A dad troubled by aches but bearing up courageously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns PA into AP; 'brave' is a noun, a Native American warrior, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: An Apache was a warrior of a Native American people, and such warriors are traditionally called braves.

clue.text: Things aren't what they seem, but don't ever say so

definitions.meaning: appearances can be deceptive, a saying of uncertainty
read literally: you are never able to tell, that is never able to say

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a proverb about deceptive appearances, and taken word by word it means one is never able to say.

clue.text: To deceive the captain of the Victory 'is very rash

parts.note: to fool someone is to trick or deceive them
Thomas Hardy was captain of Nelson's flagship HMS Victory at Trafalgar

explanation.surface: Tricking Nelson's flag captain would be a reckless thing to do.
explanation.walkthrough: Nelson's dying words were reputedly 'Kiss me, Hardy', said to the Victory's captain; the apostrophe before 'is' is a printing slip.
explanation.definitionFit: Foolhardy means recklessly bold, taking needless risks, a synonym.

clue.text: He takes some interest in correcting poor diets

indicators.note: correcting puts the letters right by rearranging them, as one corrects a misprint

explanation.surface: A nutritionist with an interest in improving bad eating habits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'correcting' rearranges POOR DIETS; 'in' is a link. 'interest' is bank interest, not curiosity.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who puts money in a bank account earns interest on those savings.

clue.text: To join the union is to make an investment

definitions.meaning: read as BE A LEAGUER: to be a member of a league, an association or union
investment in its old military sense is the besieging of a town

explanation.definitionFit: Taken in parts it means to be a league member, and as a whole it means to besiege, which is to invest a fortress.

clue.text: Stick together now that the colonel has arrived

parts.note: CO, commanding officer, is a colonel's role in a regiment
someone who has arrived is here

explanation.surface: The regiment can stand united now its commanding officer is present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'now that' is a link joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To cohere is to hold together firmly as a unit, a synonym.

clue.text: Communist party organisation is given American equipment

parts.note: the apparat was the administrative machine of the Soviet Communist Party
US is short for United States, so American

explanation.surface: The Soviet party machine gets kitted out with American gear.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparatus is the equipment or gear needed for a task, a synonym.

clue.text: In total agreement, but it's of little importance

definitions.meaning: as in saying something makes no difference to one

explanation.definitionFit: Unanimous people are united as one, and something that makes no difference to you is said to be the same either way.

clue.text: About to enter an aircraft carrier

indicators.note: to enter means to go inside, so the word for about goes inside the aircraft word

parts.note: a fighter is a military aircraft
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Something is set to land on an aircraft carrier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aircraft carrier' looks like one phrase, but the definition is just 'carrier'.
explanation.definitionFit: A freighter is a ship or plane that carries cargo, so a carrier of goods.

clue.text: The creation of a highly educated monarch

parts.note: an MA, Master of Arts, is a higher university degree
a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: The genesis of a learned sovereign.
explanation.definitionFit: The making of something is its creation or production, a synonym.

clue.text: I'm standing under false pretences

parts.note: posture is the way one stands, one's stance

explanation.surface: Someone admits holding a position on false grounds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'under' is a link. The surface plays on the phrase 'under false pretences'.
explanation.definitionFit: An imposture is a deception in which someone pretends to be another, a synonym for pretence.

clue.text: Animated inclusion of vital points in the finale

indicators.note: inclusion of tells us the following pieces are taken into another word
in shows where the included pieces go: inside the word for the finale

parts.note: the end is the finale
live means living, vital
N is north, a point of the compass
E is east, a second compass point

explanation.surface: A lively performance with energetic moments in its closing number.
explanation.walkthrough: LIVE plus N and E (two compass points) go inside END after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To enliven is to make lively, so animated people or things have been made more lively.

clue.text: How graduates advance slowly but surely

definitions.meaning: graduates progress through their university degrees
gradually, a step at a time

explanation.definitionFit: Degrees are university qualifications, and the idiom means gradually, step by step.

clue.text: What mendicants do in Bournemouth, for instance

parts.note: B is the initial of Bournemouth, taken as its abbreviation
eg, exempli gratia, means for instance

explanation.surface: Beggars working the streets of an English seaside resort.
explanation.walkthrough: Loose wordplay: the place stands for its initial B, giving B, EG, as if the town were an example of the letter; Bournemouth is a south-coast English resort. 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Mendicants are beggars, who ask for alms.

clue.text: The snake in the boardroom

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the following words

explanation.surface: A serpent loose in the company boardroom.
explanation.definitionFit: A boa is a large constricting snake.

clue.text: Dress up. Understood?

indicators.note: in a down answer up means the word for dress reads from the bottom

parts.note: to tog is to dress, as in togged up

explanation.surface: An order to put on smart clothes, then a check it was followed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dress up' looks like one phrase but 'up' signals the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: To get something is to understand it, so got means understood.

clue.text: Do freer monopoly arrangements lead to an easy profit?

indicators.note: arrangements shows the letters of the preceding words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking whether relaxing monopoly deals makes money easy to come by.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes payment for very little effort, a windfall.

clue.text: To go on the stage is the done thing

explanation.definitionFit: To perform in theatre is to act, and a deed is an act.

clue.text: Fruits which survive in very spacious surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings means the word for very spacious goes around another

parts.note: OS, outsize, is a label for very large clothes
one who survives lives on

explanation.surface: Produce that lasts well in roomy storage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'which' and 'in' are links. OS (outsize) is a clothing size mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Olives are small oily fruits of the olive tree.

clue.text: Touch the doorknob

definitions.meaning: the part of a door you grip

explanation.definitionFit: To handle is to touch with the hands, and a door handle is its knob.

clue.text: Just a little soda, but it's a sensation

definitions.meaning: a small dash of soda water added to a drink
a big stir, as in making headlines

explanation.definitionFit: A dash of mixer added to whisky is a small quantity, and a stir in the newspapers is a front-page sensation.

clue.text: Support for young Fido

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
Fido is a typical dog's name, and a young dog is a pup

explanation.surface: Help for a puppy.
explanation.definitionFit: To prop up is to hold up or bolster, a phrasal synonym.

clue.text: Playing a poor role with a poor spirit

definitions.meaning: performing an inferior part on stage
taking something amiss, with ill feeling

explanation.definitionFit: Literally an actor cast in a weak part, and idiomatically taking a remark badly, with offence.

clue.text: Other people admit an alternative proposition

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the word for alternative goes inside

parts.note: they means other people
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: Others concede that there is another idea.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory is a proposed explanation, a proposition to be tested.

clue.text: They throw light on the way people drive

definitions.text: They throw light on the way people drive

parts.words: They throw light on the way people drive
parts.note: sounds like critics of driving habits, but literally describes lamps lighting the road ahead of cars

explanation.definitionFit: Car headlights illuminate the road along which motorists travel.

clue.text: The midshipman who has one is going to pot

definitions.text: The midshipman who has one is going to pot

parts.words: The midshipman who has one is going to pot
parts.note: one word means both a junior naval officer, in old slang, and a cannabis cigarette, smoked by someone going to pot

explanation.definitionFit: The word is old naval slang for a midshipman, and also slang for a marijuana cigarette.

clue.text: A melancholy old schoolmaster might put his capital into them

definitions.text: might put his capital into them

parts.note: blue means sad or melancholy
Mr Chips is the elderly schoolmaster of James Hilton's novel Goodbye, Mr Chips

explanation.surface: A sad elderly teacher investing his savings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' is a link; 'capital' is money to invest. Mr Chips is a fictional English public-school master.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue chips are shares in large, reliable companies, a safe home for invested money.
